claims.text: The material family of interest is multiphase refractory high-entropy alloys.
The primary mechanical property of interest is tensile ductility during or after aging.
W-Ta-Ni-Fe and Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloys are example systems relevant to the proposed study.
The initial alloy can be solutionized or as-cast and contain a matrix phase before substantial precipitation.
The initial state contains a minor fraction of disordered solute clusters prior to significant chemical ordering.
The relevant chemical ordering involves D0a or D022 structures.
Stepwise aging induces nucleation, growth, and coarsening of coherent ordered precipitates such as δ lamellae or γ″ particles.
A representative treatment is aging at 650 °C for 20 hours followed by aging at 800 °C for extended durations.
The proposed aging-temperature range is 600–900 °C.
Mechanical testing should use strain rates of approximately 10^-4 to 10^-3 s^-1.
Aging should be conducted under an inert atmosphere to prevent oxidation.
Precipitate volume fraction, size, coherency, and associated lattice-misfit fields are the structural mediators of mechanical behavior.
The unaged disordered matrix is initially ductile.
Coherent ordered precipitates produce order hardening and lattice misfit that impede dislocation glide.
Stress concentrations at precipitate–matrix interfaces cause an intermediate brittle state with reduced ductility.
Further aging or higher temperature restores ductility through precipitate coarsening and coherency loss or through activation of precipitate shearing, twinning, or cross-slip.
Tensile ductility follows a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile trajectory as aging time or temperature increases.
Ultimate tensile strength may peak in the intermediate brittle regime.
Aging above the order-disorder transition temperature dissolves the ordered phase and prevents the brittle transition.
The transition requires coherent precipitates, while incoherent precipitates may cause immediate embrittlement without subsequent ductility recovery.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that precipitate coarsening and reduced coherency can relieve stress concentrations and restore ductility, whereas the boundary states that incoherent precipitates may cause immediate embrittlement without recovery. The effect of coherency loss is therefore specified in opposite directions without conditions that reconcile the two statements.
